title: Securities Trading Policy

tiers.name: Personnel
tiers.description: All personnel of the Group, including all directors, officers, employees, contractors and consultants, including all Personnel that work regularly at any of the Group's offices regardless of their working arrangements. Subject to Permitted Trading Windows, clearance or notification before dealing, no speculative short-term trading, no hedging or derivatives dealing without prior written approval, and no margin lending; differentiated only by which Authorising Officer must approve or be notified.

tiers.description: Clearance table row: gives prior written notice of intention to deal to the Company Secretary, rather than seeking approval.

tiers.name: Associates
tiers.description: Associates as defined in the Corporations Act 2001 (Cth), including close family members of any Personnel and any trust or entities controlled by any Personnel. Personnel must, to the extent able, ensure their Associates comply with the policy.

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Board may declare 'any other period as the board of directors of the Company (Board) may decide' as an additional Permitted Trading Window, and separately 'may also impose an ad hoc prohibited period during a trading window specified above'. The Policy does not state whether an ad hoc prohibited period is itself confidential, though refusal or withdrawal of an individual's clearance to trade must be kept confidential (6.4).

rules.detail: 'Securities' is defined to include 'other derivatives relating to the shares', and clause 6.8 expressly names dealing in derivatives (warrants, equity swaps, put and call options, CFDs) as requiring prior written approval from the Authorising Officer before entry.
rules.evidence: Personnel and their Associates must not, without prior written approval by the relevant Authorising Officer specified in paragraph 6.4, engage in hedging arrangements, deal in derivatives or enter into other arrangements which vary economic risk related to PEXA Securities including, for example, dealing in warrants, equity swaps, put and call options, contracts for difference and other contracts intended to secure a profit or avoid a loss based on fluctuations in the price of PEXA Securities.

rules.detail: Unlike policies that ban hedging of unvested equity outright, PEXA extends the same prior-written-approval regime to unvested securities rather than prohibiting it.
rules.evidence: This provision includes engaging in hedging or other arrangements that would have the effect of limiting the economic risk in connection with PEXA Securities including securities which are unvested, subject to a holding lock or issued pursuant to an equity based remuneration scheme.

rules.detail: Same prior-written-approval regime extends to vested securities that remain subject to a holding lock, rather than an outright ban.
rules.evidence: This provision includes engaging in hedging or other arrangements that would have the effect of limiting the economic risk in connection with PEXA Securities including securities which are unvested, subject to a holding lock or issued pursuant to an equity based remuneration scheme.

rules.detail: General hedging prohibition (subject to prior written approval) applies to any PEXA Securities without a vesting-state limitation.
rules.evidence: Personnel and their Associates must not, without prior written approval by the relevant Authorising Officer specified in paragraph 6.4, engage in hedging arrangements, deal in derivatives or enter into other arrangements which vary economic risk related to PEXA Securities.

rules.detail: Monetisation is not named, but the broad catch-all for 'other arrangements which vary economic risk' and 'other contracts intended to secure a profit or avoid a loss based on fluctuations in the price of PEXA Securities' would sweep in a prepaid forward sale or similar monetisation structure, requiring prior written approval.
rules.evidence: enter into other arrangements which vary economic risk related to PEXA Securities ... and other contracts intended to secure a profit or avoid a loss based on fluctuations in the price of PEXA Securities

rules.detail: Short selling is not named, but is inherently speculative trading and would fall within the no-speculative-trading restriction; a waiver under 6.6 is available for exceptional circumstances.
rules.evidence: Personnel and their Associates should not trade in PEXA Securities on a short term basis or for speculative trading gain.

rules.detail: Securities lending is not mentioned anywhere in the Policy.
Contracts for difference are expressly named as an example of hedging/derivative dealing requiring prior written approval.
rules.evidence: including, for example, dealing in warrants, equity swaps, put and call options, contracts for difference and other contracts intended to secure a profit or avoid a loss based on fluctuations in the price of PEXA Securities

rules.detail: Outright ban with no approval carve-out, expressly covering entry into the arrangement, transferring shares into a margin loan account, and selling shares to satisfy a margin call.
rules.evidence: Any dealing in PEXA Securities by any Personnel pursuant to a margin lending arrangement is not permitted. Such dealings would cover: any dealing into a margin lending arrangement in respect of PEXA Securities; transferring PEXA Securities in the Company into an existing margin loan account; and selling PEXA Securities in the Company to satisfy a call pursuant to a margin loan.

rules.detail: Granting security is not named as such; the margin lending ban necessarily prohibits granting security over PEXA Securities as collateral for a loan. Unlike comparable ASX policies, there is no Annexure carve-out excluding a secured lender's enforcement sale from the trading restrictions, so pledging shares carries real risk of breach on any forced sale.
rules.evidence: Any dealing in PEXA Securities by any Personnel pursuant to a margin lending arrangement is not permitted.

rules.detail: The ban is confined in terms to 'margin lending arrangement[s]', not 'any other secured financing arrangement' generally, leaving some scope to argue a bespoke bank loan not documented as a margin loan sits outside the literal wording; but 6.8's broad economic-risk language and the absence of any secured-lender carve-out in the Annexure create real risk it would still be caught or refused.
rules.evidence: Any dealing in PEXA Securities by any Personnel pursuant to a margin lending arrangement is not permitted.

rules.detail: Phrased as 'should not' rather than 'must not', but the exceptional-circumstances waiver process (6.6) treats it as a binding compliance provision capable of being waived. No specific holding period is defined.
rules.evidence: Personnel and their Associates should not trade in PEXA Securities on a short term basis or for speculative trading gain.

exemption_authority: A waiver from compliance with the Permitted Trading Window/clearance provisions (6.4) or the no-speculative-short-term-trading rule (6.5) may be granted by the relevant Authorising Officer for severe financial hardship, court order, or other circumstances the Authorising Officer deems exceptional, for a duration of 5 trading days (or such other period notified). No broader exemption authority is stated.

bespoke_clauses.clause: engage in hedging arrangements, deal in derivatives or enter into other arrangements which vary economic risk related to PEXA Securities including, for example, dealing in warrants, equity swaps, put and call options, contracts for difference and other contracts intended to secure a profit or avoid a loss based on fluctuations in the price of PEXA Securities
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Put and call options, and 'other contracts intended to secure a profit or avoid a loss based on fluctuations in the price of PEXA Securities', are expressly named as requiring prior written approval – an OTC equity collar with a bank is squarely and expressly caught, not merely swept in by a general dealing definition.

bespoke_clauses.topic: hedging permitted with approval, even pre-vesting
bespoke_clauses.clause: This provision includes engaging in hedging or other arrangements that would have the effect of limiting the economic risk in connection with PEXA Securities including securities which are unvested, subject to a holding lock or issued pursuant to an equity based remuneration scheme.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Unlike many peer policies that flatly ban hedging of unvested or holding-locked equity, PEXA only requires prior written approval from the Authorising Officer even for unvested or locked securities, leaving room in principle for a cleared collar over such securities subject to the Authorising Officer's discretion.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Any dealing in PEXA Securities by any Personnel pursuant to a margin lending arrangement is not permitted. Such dealings would cover: ... selling PEXA Securities in the Company to satisfy a call pursuant to a margin loan.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Unlike typical ASX policies, PEXA's Annexure of excluded dealings contains no carve-out for a secured lender's forced sale; a margin call sale is itself listed as a prohibited dealing, so the bank could not rely on enforcement/forced sale rights without exposing the executive to a policy breach.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Any dealing in PEXA Securities by any Personnel pursuant to a margin lending arrangement is not permitted.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The prohibition is confined to 'margin lending arrangement[s]'; it does not extend in terms to 'any other secured financing arrangement', so a bespoke bank loan secured by a pledge of the collared shares that is not documented as a margin loan may sit outside the literal wording, though the breadth of 6.8's 'vary economic risk' language creates residual risk it would still require, or be refused, approval.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Any clearance to trade can be given, withdrawn or refused by the Company in its discretion without giving any reasons ... If clearance to trade PEXA Securities is refused, the person seeking the clearance must keep that information confidential and not disclose it to anyone.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Clearance for a collar trade is entirely discretionary, revocable without reasons, and any refusal must be kept confidential from the bank counterparty, adding execution uncertainty.

bespoke_clauses.clause: in the case of Directors, provided with sufficient information to enable the Company to comply with its ASX reporting obligations ... no later than five business days after the date of the change. The Company requires the notification to reach the Reporting Officer within 3 days of the trade or other change of interest.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A Director's collar trade will need to be reported to ASX within the standard change-of-interest timeframe, and the Company requires internal notice within 3 days, both of which the bank's documentation timetable needs to accommodate.

summary: A funded collar faces two distinct hurdles under this policy. The derivative leg is expressly addressed: 'Securities' includes 'other derivatives relating to the shares', and clause 6.8 expressly names put and call options and 'other contracts intended to secure a profit or avoid a loss based on fluctuations in the price of PEXA Securities' as requiring prior written approval from the relevant Authorising Officer (the Chair of the Audit and Risk Committee for the Board Chair, the Chair of the Board for other Directors and the CEO, or the CEO for direct-report Senior Executives) before entry – notably, this approval requirement applies even to hedging unvested or holding-locked equity rather than banning it outright. The loan leg is the harder problem: clause 6.9 bans 'any dealing in PEXA Securities ... pursuant to a margin lending arrangement' outright, expressly including 'selling PEXA Securities ... to satisfy a call pursuant to a margin loan', and unlike comparable ASX policies there is no Annexure carve-out for a secured lender's forced sale, so a bank's enforcement sale of pledged shares would itself breach the policy. The ban's wording is limited to a 'margin lending arrangement', leaving some scope to argue a bespoke, non-margin-loan security interest falls outside it, but this is a real interpretive risk given the policy's broad hedging language and the absence of any forced-sale exception. Overall, the derivative legs of a collar can likely be cleared with prior written approval outside a prohibited trading period, but the secured-loan leg cannot be structured to survive an enforcement event without breaching the policy, making a genuinely funded (as opposed to unfunded) collar very difficult to implement safely.
